READ-ONLY audit. Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (branch feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info). Do NOT edit any file, do NOT run git mutations, do NOT write any report file. Return findings as your final text message only.

I am auditing whether feature SFCC-89 conforms to the Vitest conventions established by the already-merged PR #59 (SFCC-55, global footer).

YOUR SCOPE: **Vitest test shape and test-coverage criteria only.** Not stories, not styling.

BASELINE (PR #59, merged into develop, in the tree now):
- overrides/app/components/footer/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts
- overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
- overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/utils/isSafeHref.test.ts (if present)
- overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.test.ts (if present — find it)
Find any other *.test.ts(x) that PR #59 added: `git diff develop~12..develop --stat -- '*.test.ts' '*.test.tsx'` may help, and `git log --oneline develop~14..develop` shows its commits. The merge commit is 8362b3c.

UNDER AUDIT (SFCC-89, new on this branch — `git diff develop...HEAD --stat`):
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductModelInfo/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
- overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.test.ts
- overrides/app/utils/richText.test.tsx
- overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx (modified, +15 lines — see what was added)

Note which SFCC-89 components have NO test: zimmProductName, zimmProductContent, and the extracted partial pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx.

Also read .claude/rules/testing.md in full — especially the paragraph beginning "This is not license to skip a component's own test file" and the "Known gap: ZimmIcon throws under Vitest" note, since those are the written criteria.

COMPARE ON EXACTLY THESE AXES, verdict CONSISTENT / DIVERGENT / "#59 ITSELF INCONSISTENT" for each:

1. **Which components get a test, and on what criterion.** Reconstruct the *implicit rule* #59 applied: which of its components have an index.test.tsx and which don't, and what distinguishes them (branching logic? prop→JSX decisions? event wiring? pure interpolation?). Then apply that same reconstructed rule to each SFCC-89 component and say whether the presence/absence of a test file is consistent. Pay particular attention to zimmProductName and zimmProductContent (no tests) and staticProductHeader.tsx (no test) — read those three source files and judge whether #59's criterion would have demanded a test. testing.md explicitly says pure-interpolation components like BottomBar are exempt; is that the situation here, or do these have real branching?

2. **What the tests assert.** #59's assertion style vs SFCC-89's: querying by role/accessible name vs text vs testid vs class; asserting rendered output vs asserting internal implementation calls; whether style/recipe values are asserted (and if so how). Give concrete examples with file:line + anchor text from both sides.

3. **Mocking policy.** What #59 mocks and at what surface (`vi.mock` of ZimmIcon per the testing.md known gap? mocking child components? mocking hooks?). What SFCC-89 mocks. Is the granularity the same ("smallest possible surface")? Does either mock the thing under test?

4. **Test file structure.** `describe`/`it` vs `test`; `beforeEach`/`afterEach` presence and what they do (`vi.clearAllMocks`); render helpers — does either side have or need a `renderWithProviders`; is there duplicated wrapper boilerplate per test file; are the two sides using the same render wrapper approach (ChakraProvider? IntlProvider? bare `render`?). Note: testing.md says a `useIntl` consumer MUST be wrapped or it throws.

5. **Cross-cutting guard tests.** #59 added `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (a guard that walks the registered recipe map). SFCC-89 added `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (a NEW guard file in a different location) and modified `theme/index.test.tsx`. Read recipeParts.test.ts and recipeGuards.test.ts carefully and report: (a) what exactly does recipeParts.test.ts guard, (b) does it overlap/duplicate recipeGuards.test.ts, (c) should it have been added to the existing recipeGuards.test.ts instead of a new file in a new location, (d) does the new file's location (`components/ui-kits/` rather than `theme/components/`) follow any established precedent. This is a high-priority question.

6. **Do the tests actually run and pass?** Run `npx vitest run` scoped to the relevant paths (read-only, safe) — e.g. `npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits overrides/app/pages/product-detail overrides/app/utils/richText.test.tsx overrides/app/theme` — and report pass/fail counts and any failures. Do NOT run `npm start`. If vitest takes too long, scope it more narrowly. Also report total test count added by SFCC-89.

CRITICAL METHOD NOTES:
- Cite **file:line PLUS anchor text** for every claim; line numbers have drifted repeatedly here.
- I care most about a divergence that is **UNIFORM across SFCC-89** — six per-commit reviews already caught the one-offs. Label each finding UNIFORM or ONE-OFF.
- Where #59 is itself inconsistent, say which variant SFCC-89 followed and whether that was the better choice.
- Do not audit design values / Figma fidelity — conventions only.
- Already settled, do not re-raise: aria-live is deliberately on the price element rather than a hidden sibling; useUiCopy was deliberately removed from the style-code label.

Be thorough — read every file listed. Return a structured comparison, not a vague summary.</prompt>
</invoke>

Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

# SFCC-89 vs PR #59 (SFCC-55) — Vitest conventions audit

## Baseline reconstruction

PR #59 (merge `8362b3c`) added **14** test files. The full set, for the record:

`footer/index.test.tsx`, `footer/footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx`, `ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx`, `ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts`, `uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx`, `hooks/useSubscribeSection.test.ts`, `hooks/useUiCopy.test.tsx`, `hooks/useZimmModal.test.tsx`, `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.test.ts`, `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, `theme/fontFace.test.tsx`, `utils/resolveByRegion.test.ts`, `utils/safeHref.test.ts` (**not** `isSafeHref.test.ts` — the file is `safeHref.test.ts`), plus a 4-line edit to `theme/index.test.tsx`. `hooks/useUiCopy.test.tsx` is `.tsx`, not `.ts`.

SFCC-89 adds **8** files / **107** test cases: `richText.test.tsx` 63, `productInfo.test.ts` 15, `recipeParts.test.ts` 8, `zimmProductMeta` 6, `zimmProductDescription` 4, `zimmProductModelInfo` 4, `zimmProductPrice` 4, `zimmProductStyleCode` 3. `theme/index.test.tsx` gains **0 new cases** — the +15 lines are 3 `expect` calls appended inside the existing `'…components'` test.

---

## Axis 1 — Which components get a test · **DIVERGENT (one component), otherwise CONSISTENT**

**#59's implicit rule**, read off what did and didn't get a file:

| #59 component | Own Vitest? | Branching present | Where coverage actually lives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `footer/index.tsx` | ✔ | fetch + region scoping | own file; exports pure `scopeToRegion` |
| `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx` | ✔ | `showContactChannels` prop branch | own file; exports pure `hasIntentionalLineBreak` |
| `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx` | ✔ | 4 hook-state branches | own file (hook mocked) |
| `footer/bottomBar/index.tsx` | ✗ | none — pure interpolation | testing.md's named exemption |
| `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:35` `if (href && isSafeHref(href))` | ✗ | yes | 2 story plays + `utils/safeHref.test.ts` |
| `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:62` `isSafeHref(href) ? (` | ✗ | yes | **another component's Vitest file** (`footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:68-88`) + 2 plays |
| `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:37` `useState`, `:47` `if (!value)` | ✗ | yes, plus state | 4 story plays |
| `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` | ✗ | yes | `useZimmModal.test.tsx` + footer plays |

So #59's operative criterion was **narrower than testing.md as written**: a Vitest file when the render branch is driven by something only a mock can produce (a hook return, a fetch result), or when a pure helper is exported alongside; plain-prop branching went to a story `play`.

**`#59 ITSELF INCONSISTENT` here.** `zimmContactIconRow` has real branching, no own test file, and its `aria-label`/`href` contract is asserted from `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:78-80` — the exact "relying on a *different* component's file" pattern testing.md's *"This is not license to skip a component's own test file"* paragraph prohibits, in the same PR that paragraph cites as its reference example.

**SFCC-89 followed the stricter variant, and that was the better choice** (UNIFORM):

- `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:21` `if (isBlankRichText(description)) return null` → own file ✔
- `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:29` same shape → own file ✔
- `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:35` `if (!price) return null` → own file ✔ — a **plain-prop** branch that #59 would have left to a play (cf. `zimmNavItem`)
- `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:29` `if (!value) return null` → own file ✔ — same
- `zimmProductMeta/index.tsx:43` `if (isBlankRichText(modelInfo) && !styleCode) return null` → own file ✔ — the only genuinely load-bearing guard in the set (its recipe carries an unconditional `paddingTop`), correctly identified as such in the file docstring at `index.test.tsx:16-21`

### The three untested components

**`zimmProductName` — CONSISTENT, no test correctly.** `index.tsx:27-35` is `useStyleConfig` + one `return`. Zero conditionals; `as` is a pure passthrough. This is the BottomBar exemption exactly. Heading role/level is covered by 2 story plays, and `theme/index.test.tsx` now pins its registration.

**`zimmProductContent` — CONSISTENT, no test correctly.** `index.tsx:34-43` is `useStyleConfig` + three unconditional children. No branching; each child owns its own collapse. 4 story plays assert the flex column's child count and rhythm. Exemption applies.

**`staticProductHeader.tsx` — DIVERGENT. This is the finding.** It is not pure interpolation; it has five prop→JSX decisions:

```
:55   const info = selectPdpProductInfo(headerProduct ?? { name }, …)
:59   {headerCategory && (
:80   <Skeleton isLoaded={Boolean(info)} minHeight="var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)">
:91   price={isProductPartOfBundle ? undefined : info.price}
:97   {!isProductPartOfBundle && (
:99   {headerProduct?.productPromotions && <PromoCallout product={headerProduct} />}
```

Under #59's own criterion this is the `FooterNavColumn` case (prop-driven branching → own Vitest file), and it is the component in SFCC-89 with the most decision logic. It has 3 story plays instead.

Worse, **`isProductPartOfBundle: true` is exercised nowhere in any layer.** `grep -rn isProductPartOfBundle` over `pages/product-detail` and `ui-kits` returns only `stories.tsx:34` (an `argTypes` control), `stories.tsx:65` `false`, `stories.tsx:95` `false`. So the price-suppression at `:91` and the promo gate at `:97` — the two branches whose in-file comments explicitly justify their existence ("without this the price would be the one part of that header which stopped being gated") — have zero coverage. There are also no PDP Playwright specs on this branch (`e2e/tests/zimm/` contains only `homepage/`; the `test(pdp)` commits are on a different branch), so nothing downstream picks it up either.

---

## Axis 2 — What the tests assert · **DIVERGENT (uniform), defensible**

### Selector strategy — the clearest uniform divergence

| File | `ByTestId` | `ByRole` |
|---|---|---|
| `footer/footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` | 0 | 6 |
| `footer/index.test.tsx` | 0 | 1 |
| `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` | 0 | 17 |
| `zimmProductDescription/index.test.tsx` | 3 | 0 |
| `zimmProductModelInfo/index.test.tsx` | 2 | 0 |
| `zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx` | 2 | 0 |
| `zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx` | 2 | 0 |
| `zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx` | 13 | 0 |

**#59 used zero test IDs across three component test files; SFCC-89 uses them exclusively across five.** `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:56` `screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Our Story' })`, `:87` `screen.getByLabelText('Call us')`; `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:87` `getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i })`, `:105` `getByRole('alert')`. Against `zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx:19` `screen.getByTestId('product-style-code').textContent`, `zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx:53` `screen.getByTestId('product-meta')`.

**Largely justified, not simply a lapse.** Four of the five SFCC-89 components render a role-less `chakra.div`/`chakra.p` (`zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:25`, `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:33`, `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:59`, `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:32`), so no role query exists; and the collapse assertions need a node handle for something that renders *nothing*, which text queries can't provide. The `data-testid`s are also already in the production DOM for the E2E layer (commit `5a56e72` "add E2E testids"), so the tests reuse an existing affordance rather than adding one. `getByText` is available and used once (`zimmProductDescription/index.test.tsx:35`). Worth stating in the PR body as a deliberate choice, because a reviewer coming from #59 will read 13 test IDs in one file as drift.

### Output vs implementation calls

Both sides assert injected-callback invocation, which is contract not implementation: `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:145` `expect(handleEmailSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith('shopper@example.com')` vs `productInfo.test.ts:85-86` `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` / `toHaveBeenCalledWith(895, 'AUD')`. CONSISTENT.

One **ONE-OFF** exception: `zimmProductDescription/index.test.tsx:49-58`, `'asks isBlankRichText before parsing, and passes the raw value through unchanged'`, asserts only `expect(isBlankRichText).toHaveBeenCalledWith(raw)` / `expect(parseRichText).toHaveBeenCalledWith(raw)`. These are internal-collaborator call assertions where an output assertion would do (return a distinctive node from the mock and assert it rendered), and the *"before"* in the test name is never asserted — there is no ordering check. The pattern doesn't repeat in the other four files.

### Style / recipe values — different location for an existing pattern

- #59 put recipe assertions in a dedicated `<name>.css.test.ts`, calling the recipe function directly: `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:87` `ZimmTextInput.baseStyle({ ...base, hasError: true }).row.borderBottom`, `:102` `floated.top` `toBe('var(--zimm-scale-3xs)')`. No `getComputedStyle` in any #59 component test.
- SFCC-89 ships **zero `.css.test.ts` files for 7 new recipes** and instead puts one computed-style assertion inside a component test: `zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx:113-115` `window.getComputedStyle(screen.getByTestId('product-meta'))` → `.gap` `toBe('1.75rem')`, `.paddingTop` `toBe('1.75rem')`.

**Verdict: CONSISTENT on the absence of `.css.test.ts`** — `zimmTextInput.css.ts` earned its own suite because it is a function-form `baseStyle` over five booleans with a colour cascade; every SFCC-89 recipe is a plain-object `baseStyle` (`zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:19` is a nullary function returning a constant; `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:20` has a single-entry `variants` map). Nothing to branch, nothing to test. **The `getComputedStyle` idiom is not new to the repo** — `theme/index.test.tsx:337-362` (`describe('rendered output')`, added by `fe04791`, pre-dating #59) already uses `ChakraProvider` + `window.getComputedStyle` + `getByTestId`. SFCC-89 relocated it into the component's own folder, which is the *better* placement per testing.md's discoverability argument.

### DOM-position assertions — new, no #59 analogue (ONE-OFF ×2)

`zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx:39-40` `container.querySelectorAll('[aria-live]')` `toHaveLength(1)` / `container.firstChild` `toBe(price)`; `zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx:61-62` `root.children[0]` / `root.children[1]`. Both carry in-file justification (`:58-60` "By position, not just presence"). Legitimate — order genuinely isn't observable any other way under a symmetrical `gap` — but they couple to DOM shape: any wrapper element inserted between root and children breaks them. #59's closest analogue is `toBeEmptyDOMElement()` (`footer/index.test.tsx:153, 172, 181, 219`), which SFCC-89 also uses (`zimmProductPrice:52`, `zimmProductMeta:91`).

## Axis 3 — Mocking policy · **DIVERGENT in idiom (uniform), CONSISTENT in granularity**

**Surfaces mocked.** #59: the `ZimmIcon` known gap (`footer/index.test.tsx:12-14`, `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:14-21`, `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:12-16`); hooks (`use-multi-site`, `useContentfulClient`, `useSubscribeSection`, `useUiCopy`, `useContentfulEntries`); one child component (`zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:23-39`). SFCC-89: only `app/utils/richText` — a **utility**, a surface #59 never mocked (it tested `safeHref`/`resolveByRegion` for real and let consumers use the real thing).

**Granularity — CONSISTENT and correct.** SFCC-89 mocks the smallest surface, mocks nothing under test, and documents every mock. `zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx:11-14` is the strongest instance in either PR: it uses `mockImplementation` rather than `mockReturnValue` specifically so a molecule that dropped `modelInfo` or handed the guard `styleCode` would fail — *"a fixed return ignores its argument"*. It also deliberately leaves the two child atoms **real** (`:12-14`) because composition order is the contract, which is a more considered call than #59's blanket child-stub in `zimmSubscribeSection`. No SFCC-89 file mocks its own subject. No `ZimmIcon` mock is needed — none of these components renders an icon; correctly omitted rather than copied.

**The idiom differs, uniformly, across all three files that mock (`zimmProductDescription:14-19`, `zimmProductModelInfo:14-19`, `zimmProductMeta:28-33`):**

```ts
// SFCC-89 — module-scope handles, factory delegates
const parseRichText = vi.fn();
vi.mock('app/utils/richText', () => ({ parseRichText: (html) => parseRichText(html), … }));
import { ZimmProductDescription } from './index';   // ← import placed AFTER the consts, line 21
```
```ts
// #59 — vi.fn() inside the factory, typed handle via vi.mocked
vi.mock('app/hooks/useContentfulClient', () => ({ useContentfulClient: vi.fn() }));
const mockUseContentfulClient = vi.mocked(useContentfulClient);   // footer/index.test.tsx:20-30
```

**This is a real fragility, UNIFORM.** SFCC-89's version only works because Vitest's SSR transform rewrites ESM imports in place rather than hoisting them — the `import { ZimmProductDescription } from './index'` at line 21 must execute *after* the `const … = vi.fn()` on lines 14-15, or the mock factory hits those bindings in TDZ. It relies on non-standard-ESM ordering, and `import/first`-style lint rules normally flag the misplaced import. The idiomatic fix is `vi.hoisted()`; #59's factory-internal `vi.fn()` + `vi.mocked()` sidesteps the question entirely and is also better typed (SFCC-89's handles are untyped `vi.fn()`). Recommend converting to either #59's pattern or `vi.hoisted()`.

## Axis 5 — Cross-cutting guard tests · **DIVERGENT — highest-priority item**

### (a) What `recipeParts.test.ts` guards

For every `*.css.ts` under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**` that declares a `parts:` array, it regex-extracts that array (`:31`), regex-extracts every `styles.X` / `styles['X']` read from the **sibling `index.tsx`** (`:33`, `:62-65`), and asserts the read set ⊆ the declared set (`:78-79`). Plus a vacuity guard at `:85-89`, correctly modelled on `recipeGuards.test.ts:287-293`. 8 tests = 7 recipes + the guard. It also handles a missing sibling as recorded data rather than a throw (`:41-47`) so a collection error can't take the vacuity guard down with it — a genuinely well-thought-out detail.

### (b) Overlap with `recipeGuards.test.ts` — **none. No duplication.**

`recipeGuards.test.ts` walks the *composed runtime theme object* (`import theme from '../index'`, `import { components } from './index'`) for five things: bare spacing keys on sizing props (`:295`), bare keys on typography props (`:305`), bare keys inside compound shorthands (`:315`), bare registered-scale keys as house style (`:331`), and silent base-SFCC recipe inheritance (`:347`). `grep -n parts recipeGuards.test.ts` hits only lines 321-322 (a local variable named `parts`, unrelated) and a comment at 350. **There is no parts-vs-reads check anywhere in it.** Different mechanism too: object walk vs source-text regex.

**But `recipeParts.test.ts:15-16` states the opposite and is wrong:**

> `Scope: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**. Recipes elsewhere are covered by theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts.`

For *this* guard's concern they are not covered — by that file or any other. Concretely, three multipart recipes sit outside the walk and are unguarded:

- `footer/footer.css.ts` — consumed by `footer/index.tsx:91-124` (`styles.container`, `.main`, `.contentRow`, `.subscribe`, `.links`, `.linksInner`, `.logo`, `.logoButton`)
- `footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`
- `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`

Of the 10 multipart recipes in `overrides/`, the guard sees 7 (5 from #59, 2 from SFCC-89). **The docstring claim should be corrected or the scope widened to `overrides/app/components/**`** — the walk needs no change beyond the root constant, and it would then cover all 10.

**Two live blind spots inside the in-scope set:**

1. **The read regex only recognises the identifier `styles`.** `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:37` does `const chrome = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_MODAL_RECIPE, {})` and reads `chrome.actions` at `:97`. That read is invisible to `READ_RE`. (`actions` *is* declared at `zimmModal.css.ts:6`, so no live bug — the guard simply cannot see it.)
2. **A recipe is only reconciled against its sibling `index.tsx`.** `zimmModal.css.ts`'s parts are consumed from two folders (`zimmModal/index.tsx` and `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx`); only the first is checked. A cross-folder consumer reading an undeclared part passes.

**Tail-wagging-dog signal.** `zimmProductMeta.css.ts:5-9` records that the recipe was made multipart with a single `root` part *in order to be visible to this guard*: *"Multipart with a single `parts` array rather than a bare `baseStyle`: `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` … a recipe with no `parts` key is skipped by that walk entirely."* Production shape chosen to satisfy a same-PR self-authored guard. Defensible as forward-looking, worth a reviewer's eye.

### (c) Should it have gone into `recipeGuards.test.ts`?

**Genuinely arguable, and the governance answer probably wins.** `CODEOWNERS:117` routes `overrides/app/theme/components/` to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers` **and** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, whereas `CODEOWNERS:176` routes `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` to squad A + B only. Folding the check into `recipeGuards.test.ts` would drag a squad-authored test behind the designer/Tier-1 gate on every future edit — the same reasoning `overrideStyling.md` uses to justify co-locating `.css.ts` files. The two guards also share no machinery (fs/regex vs runtime object walk), so merging them buys no code reuse.

What the separate file does **not** justify is the ui-kits-only *scope* or the incorrect cross-reference. The concern's real boundary is `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` — exactly the CODEOWNERS Tier-3 glob at `CODEOWNERS:186`. Recommendation: **keep the separate file, move it to `overrides/app/components/recipeParts.test.ts`, widen `UI_KITS` to `overrides/app/components`, fix the `:15-16` docstring, and broaden `READ_RE` past the literal `styles` identifier.** That keeps the governance win and closes the footer gap in one edit.

Note also that #59 *did* have a parts check — per-component, at `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:81-84` (`'every declared part is produced by baseStyle'`). `recipeParts.test.ts:11-13` correctly explains why that form is insufficient (renaming a part in recipe and component together keeps them mutually consistent and still breaks). So the new guard is a real improvement on #59, not a duplicate of it.

### (d) Precedent for the location

Partial. `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` is precedent for a standalone guard test with no `recipeGuards.ts` source, co-located in the directory it guards. What is new is a bare `*.test.ts` at a directory containing **only** component sub-directories — neither `conventions.md`'s component-folder layout nor `testing.md`'s file-layout section describes a directory-level guard file. And the location currently *encodes* the scope limitation instead of the concern's real boundary.

### `theme/index.test.tsx` modification — partial, **semi-UNIFORM gap**

The +3 assertions pin `ZimmProductMeta`, `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductModelInfo` as `toBeTruthy()`, with a good comment on why the list stays hand-maintained rather than derived. But `theme/components/index.ts` registers **7** new recipes; four are unpinned: `ZimmProductContent`, `ZimmProductDescription`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmProductStyleCode`. The comment's own rationale — an unregistered recipe makes `useMultiStyleConfig` return `{}`, `__css={undefined}` is legal, and the element silently inherits — applies equally to all seven. `recipeParts.test.ts` cannot substitute: it reads source text and knows nothing about registration.

Sharpest instance: **`ZimmProductPrice` has no detection at all** — no registration pin, no `.css.test.ts`, its `index.stories.tsx` is the only story file in either PR with **0** `play` functions, and `index.test.tsx` asserts only `textContent` and ARIA attributes. Unregistering it is invisible to every layer. `ZimmProductContent` and `ZimmProductDescription` are at least caught in a real browser by their story plays (4 and 3 respectively). One-line fix: extend the `toBeTruthy` list to all seven.
